name: Kelela
label: Warp
lede: She quit telemarketing in 2012, gave a mixtape away free, and a decade later a mostly Berlin-made album landed at No. 17 on Pitchfork's 2023 list.

eras.title: Gaithersburg, a violin and a metal band
eras.text: Kelela Mizanekristos grew up in the Maryland suburbs on R&B, jazz and Björk, sang in a band nobody would guess, and left Washington for Los Angeles with a day job she was about to quit.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kelela · Wikipedia: Take Me Apart
years.h: Born in Washington, D.C., raised in Gaithersburg
years.p: Kelela is the only child of Ethiopian American parents. She played violin from fourth grade and sang in her school choir.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives her birth name as Kelela Mizanekristos and her birth date as June 4, 1983. In 2017 she described herself as a black woman and second-generation Ethiopian-American who grew up in the burbs listening to R&B, jazz and Björk.

years.h: Magruder High, Montgomery College, then American University
years.p: She graduated from Magruder High School in 2001, went to Montgomery College, then transferred to American University, where she sang jazz standards in local cafés.

years.src: Rolling Stone · The Ringer · Wikipedia: Kelela
years.h: She joins Dizzy Spells and sings progressive metal
years.p: After meeting [[Tosin Abasi|9edadf07-e3a3-48b4-bff0-6a5c04298f5d]], Kelela joined the indie band Dizzy Spells and sang prog metal, a long way from the R&B she would be known for.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's 2023 profile places her in D.C.'s indie and punk scenes in the Myspace era, after open mic nights in college. The Ringer's 2017 profile says she sang jazz, metal and classic R&B after school before settling on R&B.

years.h: Moves to Los Angeles
years.p: Kelela relocated to L.A., where she would meet the producers who built her first mixtape. She now lives between Los Angeles and London.

years.h: She quits telemarketing with two songs in the can
years.p: In November 2012 Kelela left her telemarketing job to make a mixtape, with two songs already recorded.

eras.title: Free, and made for the club
eras.text: Fade to Mind and Night Slugs were making warped, bass-heavy club music, mostly without singers. Kelela became the voice of that scene, and the first person to give it a hook you could cry to.

years.h: A guest verse on Teengirl Fantasy's "EFX" opens the door
years.p: Kelela sang on "EFX" from Teengirl Fantasy's Tracer, which led to Prince William of Fade to Mind. In May she appeared on [[Kingdom|2ae5ac16-1d41-464e-8fac-e856d91dd822]]'s "Bank Head".
years.xp: Prince William introduced her to the Fade to Mind sound and to its London sister label, Night Slugs. The Guardian's Harriet Gibsone later described Cut 4 Me as an experiment for the production team, the first time it had put vocals on its club tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cut 4 Me · Mixmag · Wikipedia: Kelela
years.h: Cut 4 Me: a free mixtape built over club instrumentals
years.p: Thirteen tracks on Fade to Mind, with beats from [[Kingdom|2ae5ac16-1d41-464e-8fac-e856d91dd822]], [[Nguzunguzu|de7d7191-5ca6-4e19-a69e-006a09a63df2]], [[Bok Bok|7bfc0474-c3bd-400e-bfb6-d1c66823c13d]], [[Girl Unit|a2be751d-53a5-491b-a565-80c9c3c39304]] and [[Jam City|1017c0b1-8219-4527-bc09-b32991bb8748]]. Pitchfork named it Best New Music.
years.xp:
It was a free download on SoundCloud. Kelela told Mixmag it held her first 20 completed songs, written when she was 30. The Guardian ranked it seventh among the albums of 2013, according to Wikipedia.

A deluxe edition arrived April 6, 2015, adding an interlude and eight remixes. One of its tracks, "Go All Night", also turned up on Solange Knowles's Saint Heron compilation.

years.h: "The High" goes to SoundCloud, "Melba's Call" goes to Bok Bok
years.p: Kelela put out "The High", a song from DJ Kitty Cash's Love the Free mixtape, herself on February 4. She sang on [[Bok Bok|7bfc0474-c3bd-400e-bfb6-d1c66823c13d]]'s "Melba's Call" on March 5.

eras.title: Warp, and the slow build
eras.text: Kelela signed with Warp, released an EP that told a breakup in reverse, and took four years over a debut album. Meanwhile Solange, Danny Brown and Gorillaz all wanted her voice.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hallucinogen (EP) · Wikipedia: Kelela · The Ringer
years.h: Hallucinogen tells a relationship backwards
years.p: Released by Warp and Cherry Coffee Music, with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]], Ariel Rechtshaid, Kingdom, Girl Unit and Daniel Aged producing. It runs from the end of a relationship to the start.
years.xp:
Kelela announced the EP on March 3 with "A Message" and its video; "Rewind" followed on September 2. Pitchfork named it Best New Music, and Anupa Mistry called it a sensuous, sensitive, hi-definition approach to R&B.

According to Wikipedia it reached No. 4 on Billboard's Heatseekers and Top Dance Albums charts, and Fact ranked it No. 8 of 2015.

years.h: Solange, Danny Brown and Clams Casino call
years.p: Kelela sang on "Scales" from Solange's A Seat at the Table, "From the Ground" on Danny Brown's Atrocity Exhibition and "A Breath Away" on Clams Casino's 32 Levels.

years.h: "Busted and Blue" on Gorillaz's Humanz
years.p: Kelela added vocals to "Busted and Blue" on [[Gorillaz|e21857d5-3256-4547-afb3-4b6ded592596]]'s Humanz, and appeared with Danny Brown on "Submission".

years.src: Wikipedia: Take Me Apart · Wikipedia: Kelela
yt: Enemy, Boiler Room x adidas Originals Madrid
years.h: Take Me Apart, four years in the making
years.p: Warp released the debut album on October 6, with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]] and [[Jam City|1017c0b1-8219-4527-bc09-b32991bb8748]] behind most of it. Pitchfork gave it 8.6 and ranked it No. 4 of 2017.
years.xp:
It was recorded at Heavy Duty in Burbank and at Mutant and Rooftop in London, with Kwes mixing. The lead single "LMK" arrived August 1, and "Frontline" premiered on HBO's Insecure.

Metacritic has it at 84. Stereogum's Tom Breihan called it a towering achievement of an album, and it peaked at No. 128 on the Billboard 200, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: The syllabus
eras.text: After the debut she stopped and did the reading. The remix album made producers give up their stems, and the collaborators on her next record got homework.

years.h: Remix album, on her terms: send the stems
years.p: Kaytranada, Rare Essence and Serpentwithfeet reworked Take Me Apart, and a "LMK" remix pulled in Princess Nokia, Junglepussy, Cupcakke and Ms. Boogie.
years.xp: It came out exactly a year after the album. Kelela told Mixmag that nothing would be on the project unless producers sent stems and let her do the final arrangement.

years.h: Collaborators get a reading list before they get a session
years.p: Kelela put together a primer of essays, podcasts and documentaries, from Kandis Williams on misogynoir to Safiya Umoja Noble on algorithmic oppression.
years.xp:
Mixmag calls it the syllabus for the university of her mind and says she sent it to every collaborator. The same profile says she parted with her business manager and, amicably, her publisher.

Rolling Stone asked her about the years after 2013. She called it a "post-Pitchfork era" and said there is a hierarchical value system assigned to certain sounds, which she calls sonic racism.

eras.title: Raven
eras.text: Six years after Take Me Apart, Kelela came back with a record built like a DJ set, made mostly in Berlin with the friends who had shaped her sound.

years.cap: Kelela performing at Broccoli City Festival, Washington, D.C. · Wikimedia
years.h: Berlin: 13 of Raven's 15 tracks in under two weeks
years.p: Kelela made most of the album in Berlin with OCA, Asmara Maroof of [[Nguzunguzu|de7d7191-5ca6-4e19-a69e-006a09a63df2]], [[LSDXOXO|c2710100-a9e9-46e9-bae7-4677333cd0eb]] and [[Bambii|6ca9bf1d-3992-4b77-84c9-90b88a8d0f10]]. The last track added was "Fooley", by Khalí Carela.
years.xp:
Kelela told Mixmag she met Carela at a party and, after finding his production online, told him to take it off Instagram. Asmara, a friend from her Maryland suburbs, was co-executive producer.

Wikipedia dates the recording to 2020 through 2022.

years.h: "Washed Away" is her first single in five years
years.p: Kelela released "Washed Away" with a video on September 13, 2022. Raven was announced on November 15 alongside "On the Run".

years.h: Raven: Pitchfork 8.4, Best New Music, No. 17 of 2023
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.4 and called it Best New Music, then ranked it No. 17 on its 50 Best Albums of 2023. Warp released it on February 10.
years.xp:
Eric Torres wrote in Pitchfork that it was a masterful display of tension and release. Metacritic has it at 86, and Resident Advisor put it at No. 1 for the year. Consequence had it at No. 13.

The 15 tracks run 62 minutes 33 seconds, with producers including Asmara, Yo van Lenz, LSDXOXO, Bambii, Kaytranada and Fauzia. "Contact" and "Enough for Love" were the last two singles.

years.h: "Enough for Love" on Fallon the day it comes out
years.p: Kelela performed "Enough for Love" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon on Raven's release day.

years.big: The space is dominated by Black men and light-skinned women.
years.h: Alone on the dance floor
years.p: Kelela's press statement said Raven began as a reaction to feeling alone as a Black femme working within dance music. She said this to Mixmag.
years.xp:
Kelela told Mixmag she had privileges in that space, being thin and of Ethiopian descent. She also said the Black men who get in first are, in her words, the weakest link.

The album runs its tracks together like a DJ set, moving through R&B, dancehall, drum 'n' bass and techno. In Rolling Stone she said the first half feels like summer and then it winters.

years.h: "Bury Me" on PinkPantheress's Heaven Knows
years.p: Kelela guests on "Bury Me", from [[PinkPantheress|7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d]]'s debut album Heaven Knows.

eras.title: Blue Note and a third act
eras.text: Raven's afterlife: a remix album, a Tiny Desk, a jazz-club residency, and a guitar-heavy third record with the songwriter behind PinkPantheress and Shygirl.

years.h: 20 remixes of Raven, from Shygirl to Yaeji
years.p: Singles included Karen Nyame KG's "Contact" remix and Flexulant and Bambii's "Closure". Pitchfork gave the set 7.8.

years.h: Kelela plays NPR's Tiny Desk
years.p: The Fader posted her Tiny Desk concert on February 23, 2024.

years.cap: Kelela performing at the Broccoli City Festival in Washington, D.C., 2014. · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: In the Blue Light (Kelela album)
years.h: A two-night stand at New York's Blue Note Jazz Club
years.p: Her first residency there was recorded on May 28 and 29, with arrangements by bassist and producer [[Daniel Aged|db66224d-87de-4417-9a9d-afa43151ed72]].

years.src: Wikipedia: In the Blue Light (Kelela album) · Wikipedia: Kelela
years.h: In the Blue Light: unplugged, with a harp and a jazz rhythm section
years.p: Warp released the live album from the Blue Note nights. It includes a cover of Joni Mitchell's "Furry Sings the Blues", and Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp:
The band was Daniel Aged on bass, Briley Harris on piano, Ahya Simone on harp and Buz Donald on drums, with Alayna Rodgers and Xenia Manasseh singing backup. Pitchfork's Tarisai Ngangura called her a masterful re-interpreter of her own songs.

"Better (Unplugged)" was the lead single on January 28, and a documentary film followed on February 18.

years.h: "Idea 1": grunge guitars from Oscar Scheller
years.p: Kelela's first single since Raven was written with Oscar Scheller and painter Janiva Ellis, with shoegaze guitarist Scarlet House playing on it.

years.h: New Avatar, third album on Warp
years.p: Mostly with Oscar Scheller, with A. K. Paul, Fousheé and PinkPantheress as guests. Metacritic has it at 85.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists "Outta Time", a duet with A. K. Paul that she says dates from the 2016 Take Me Apart sessions, and "The Bridge" with PinkPantheress as singles. Stereogum named it Album of the Week.

The New Avatar Live tour starts September 8, 2026, in Seattle.
